title: ParGNN: A Scalable Graph Neural Network Training Framework on multi-GPUs
problem: Full-batch Graph Neural Network training on multi-GPU systems faces severe load imbalance and high communication overhead due to irregular graph structures and uneven vertex/edge distributions.
motivation: Full-batch GNN training offers advantages in convergence accuracy and speed, but irregular load distribution and communication bottlenecks across GPUs prevent efficient scaling on multi-GPU systems.
method: ParGNN measures how much computation each GPU receives (profiling), then breaks the graph into extra pieces and redistributes them to make the work more even (graph over-partitioning and adaptive load balancing). It arranges the work in a pipeline where each GPU processes multiple graph pieces in sequence, timed so that while one GPU is computing, another is simultaneously receiving or sending data (computation-communication overlap). This keeps data flowing and GPUs busy at the same time, eliminating the idle waiting that happens when data arrives late.
key_novelty: Profile the workload to dynamically rebalance graphs across GPUs, and use pipelining to overlap data transfer with computation.
contributions: Profiler-guided adaptive load balancing with graph over-partition strategy
Subgraph pipeline algorithm overlapping communication and computation without accuracy degradation
Highest accuracy achieved with 2.7x speedup over PipeGCN and 21.8x speedup over DGL on four datasets
limitations: Scaling limit (number of GPUs) and applicability to heterogeneous GPU clusters not discussed.
primary_theme: Load-balanced full-batch GNN training with computation-communication overlap
